import type { ScriptContext, ScriptResult } from "@gtm-factory/core";

/**
 * Lead interested · distribute.you reply judge.
 *
 * Reads what the person wrote back (their words only: quoted history and our own footer stripped),
 * framed by the email we sent and the thread's subject, and asks the model for ONE label of the
 * reply-kind vocabulary. The label decides: positive (interested, asks for info, asks for a time),
 * negative (declines, wrong person, changed job, asked to stop) or neutral (anything else). A
 * person is interested when the label is positive. An answer outside the vocabulary is no verdict:
 * nothing is asserted rather than a sentiment we did not obtain.
 *
 * Provenance (business logic only; instantly-service @ 83c8f8c): src/lib/self-send/qualify-reply.ts
 * (SYSTEM_PROMPT verbatim, QUALIFICATION_EVENT_TYPES, stripQuotedHistory, subjectTheyTyped,
 * withOurOutreach, withSubject, parseQualification, qualifyReply's message assembly);
 * src/lib/reply-kind.ts (REPLY_KIND_CLASSIFICATION). v2 states the model call exactly as production sends it
 * (JSON, temperature 0, reasoning off; the LLM is the Rating's pick since LLM-PICK-SCRIPTS-1112), proven on instantly's recorded requests.
 * Left to the host: billing on the reply-judging run (platform, through the service's script door), the shadow judgment.
 *
 * Material: `reply_received` (the reply's text, the thread's subject, the email we sent).
 */
const SYSTEM_PROMPT = `You classify a single reply to a cold outreach email.

Answer with JSON only: {"classification": "<one of the labels>"}

Labels, and what each one means:
- lead_interested — they are personally interested and say so, without asking a question or proposing a time
- lead_referral — they are not the buyer themselves, but it is relevant to their company and they point you at the right person
- lead_info_requested — they want to know more: they ask a question about the offer without committing
- lead_meeting_requested — they propose or accept a specific time, or share a booking link
- lead_not_interested — they decline or say it is not relevant, WITHOUT asking to be removed
- lead_opt_out_requested — they ask to be taken off the list: "unsubscribe", "remove me", "take me off your list", "stop emailing me", "do not contact me again". Pick this over lead_not_interested whenever the reply contains a removal request, even if it also declines the offer
- lead_wrong_person — they are not the right contact and hand you nothing: no name, no relevance
- lead_changed_job — they say they have left the role or the company, so the role we wrote to is no longer theirs
- lead_out_of_office — they are away and will return; the message says nothing about the offer
- lead_neutral — anything else, including a bare acknowledgement or an unclear reply
- lead_off_topic — the conversation is about something OTHER than them buying what we sell: a partnership or reseller proposal, a job application or hiring enquiry, investors or fundraising, a vendor pitching their own product to us, or press and media. Pick this over lead_interested, lead_info_requested, lead_meeting_requested and lead_neutral whenever the exchange is about one of those rather than a purchase; our email and the subject line tell you what the conversation is about, and when our email itself offers what the reply talks about (hiring help, a partnership program, a media placement), the reply is about buying it and is NOT lead_off_topic
- lead_already_customer — they say they ALREADY buy, use or own what we offer from this company: "I already have your unit", "we're already one of your clinics", "we've been a customer for years". Pick this over every other label when they say so, even if they also ask a question. Using the same kind of product bought from ANOTHER company is not this: that is a decline
- lead_is_client — they say they ARE the company we are writing on behalf of, or work for it: "this is our own company", "I'm on the team", "you're emailing your own client"

Judge only what the reply says. Do not infer enthusiasm from politeness, and do
not treat a question about how you got their address as interest.

When the message starts with "Subject:", that is the thread's subject line. Use
it only to know what the conversation is about — never classify the subject
itself as something they wrote.

When the message carries an "Our email:" section, that is what we sent them: it
tells you what we sell. Use it only to know what the conversation is about —
never classify our words as something they wrote. Their reply is under "Their reply:".

The reply may quote our own email beneath it, and older emails of ours ended with
the words "Not relevant? Reply "stop" and I won't email you again." or "Don't want
to hear from me again? unsubscribe". That is OUR footer, not their request — only a
removal request THEY wrote is lead_opt_out_requested.

Worked examples, from real replies:
- "Stop" -> lead_opt_out_requested
- "Unsubscribe" -> lead_opt_out_requested
- "unsusbsribe" -> lead_opt_out_requested (a misspelling is still the request)
- "No interest, please stop sending emails." -> lead_opt_out_requested (the second clause asks to stop; the first alone would not)
- "Not for us, thanks." -> lead_not_interested (a decline, with no request to be removed)
- "No interest" -> lead_not_interested (declining is not asking to be taken off the list)
- Subject "Re: Acme + Beta partnership?", reply "can you explain?" -> lead_off_topic (the conversation is a partnership proposal, not a purchase)
- "Are you hiring? I'd love to join your team" -> lead_off_topic (a job enquiry)
- Our email offers job listings to employers, reply "Yes we are hiring two warehouse operatives. A free first listing sounds good. How does it work?" -> lead_info_requested (hiring is what we sell here, so this is a purchase conversation)
- "I actually am a Shockwave Centers of America clinic. I have the OTG unit. Is this email meant for those who don't have shockwave units?" -> lead_already_customer (they already own the product; the question does not make it interest)
- "We're using another brand's unit and have no need for another one" -> lead_not_interested (they bought from someone else, not from us)
- "Ha, I work at Acme, this is our own campaign" -> lead_is_client`;

const LABELS = [
  "lead_interested",
  "lead_referral",
  "lead_info_requested",
  "lead_meeting_requested",
  "lead_not_interested",
  "lead_wrong_person",
  "lead_changed_job",
  "lead_opt_out_requested",
  "lead_out_of_office",
  "lead_neutral",
  "lead_off_topic",
  "lead_already_customer",
  "lead_is_client",
];

const CLASSIFICATION: Record<string, "positive" | "negative" | "neutral"> = {
  lead_interested: "positive",
  lead_referral: "neutral",
  lead_info_requested: "positive",
  lead_meeting_requested: "positive",
  lead_not_interested: "negative",
  lead_wrong_person: "negative",
  lead_changed_job: "negative",
  lead_opt_out_requested: "negative",
  lead_neutral: "neutral",
  lead_off_topic: "neutral",
  lead_already_customer: "neutral",
  lead_is_client: "neutral",
  lead_out_of_office: "neutral",
};

export default function run(ctx: ScriptContext): ScriptResult {
  const reply = ctx.get("reply_received");
  const subject = typeof reply.content.subject === "string" ? reply.content.subject : null;
  const body = stripQuotedHistory(String(reply.content.text ?? "")).slice(0, 4000);
  const typedSubject = body ? null : subjectTheyTyped(subject);
  const stripped = body || typedSubject || "";
  if (!stripped) return null;
  const framed = withOurOutreach(stripped, typeof reply.content.ourOutreach === "string" ? reply.content.ourOutreach : null);
  const message = typedSubject ? framed : withSubject(framed, subject);
  const answer = ctx.vendor.call("llm.complete", { message, systemPrompt: SYSTEM_PROMPT, ...pickLlm(ctx, "judge"), responseFormat: "json", temperature: 0, disableThinking: true });
  if (!answer.ok) throw new Error(`llm.complete failed: ${String(answer.data.error ?? "no answer")}`);
  const kind = parseQualification(answer.data as { json?: Record<string, unknown>; content?: string });
  if (kind === null) return null;
  const classification = CLASSIFICATION[kind]!;
  return { content: { kind, classification, interested: classification === "positive" } };
}

function parseQualification(result: { json?: Record<string, unknown>; content?: string }): string | null {
  const fromJson = result.json?.classification;
  if (typeof fromJson === "string" && LABELS.includes(fromJson)) return fromJson;
  if (typeof result.content === "string") {
    try {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(result.content) as { classification?: unknown };
      if (typeof parsed.classification === "string" && LABELS.includes(parsed.classification)) return parsed.classification;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

function withOurOutreach(reply: string, ourOutreach: string | null | undefined): string {
  const ours = ourOutreach?.trim();
  return ours ? `Our email:\n${ours}\n\nTheir reply:\n${reply}` : reply;
}

function withSubject(message: string, subject: string | null | undefined): string {
  const line = subject?.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
  return line ? `Subject: ${line.slice(0, 300)}\n\n${message}` : message;
}

function subjectTheyTyped(subject: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  const line = subject?.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
  if (!line) return null;
  if (/^(re|fw|fwd|aw|wg|tr|sv|vs)\s*:/i.test(line)) return null;
  return line.slice(0, 300);
}

const QUOTED_LINE = /^\s*>/;
const ATTRIBUTION_LINE = /^\s*On .{0,120}\bwrote:\s*$/i;
const ATTRIBUTION_TAIL = /^\s*(?:\S.{0,120}\s)?wrote:\s*$/i;
const ORIGINAL_MESSAGE_LINE = /^\s*-{2,}\s*Original Message\s*-{2,}/i;
const SIGNATURE_DELIMITER = /^\s*-{2,}\s*$/;

function stripQuotedHistory(text: string): string {
  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/);
  const kept: string[] = [];
  let afterQuote = false;
  const nextNonBlankIsQuoted = (from: number): boolean => {
    for (let j = from; j < lines.length; j++) {
      if (lines[j]!.trim()) return QUOTED_LINE.test(lines[j]!);
    }
    return false;
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i]!;
    if (QUOTED_LINE.test(line)) {
      afterQuote = true;
      continue;
    }
    if (ORIGINAL_MESSAGE_LINE.test(line)) break;
    if (afterQuote && SIGNATURE_DELIMITER.test(line)) break;
    const wrappedAttribution = !ATTRIBUTION_LINE.test(line) && ATTRIBUTION_TAIL.test(line) && kept.length > 0 && /^\s*On\s/i.test(kept[kept.length - 1]!);
    if (ATTRIBUTION_LINE.test(line) || wrappedAttribution) {
      if (wrappedAttribution) kept.pop();
      if (nextNonBlankIsQuoted(i + 1)) continue;
      break;
    }
    kept.push(line);
  }
  return kept.join("\n").replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n").trim();
}


/** The LLM of one call: the Rating's pick for this Engine and this call (LLM-PICK-SCRIPTS-1112). No LLM in the Engine's universe = nothing is written: the run fails and is retried later, never a fallback model. */
function pickLlm(ctx: any, place: string, outcome?: string): { provider: string; model: string } {
  const p = ctx.vendor.call("llm.pick", outcome ? { place, outcome } : { place });
  if (!p.ok) throw new Error("llm.pick " + place + ": " + String(p.data && p.data.error) + ". Nothing is written: the run is retried later.");
  return { provider: p.data.provider, model: p.data.model };
}
